panel: 24, 26-33, 35, 15, 17 (and every node --test terminal, Boss 3/4 goal outputs)
what: The test-run, npm install and npm run terminals show output that was rewritten by a hidden sed filter (and run with a hidden --test-reporter=spec flag and a hidden `exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}`), while the shown command is the bare one. That breaks the AUTHORING house rule that any rewrite must be visible in the shown command. AUTHORING even cites js ch14 as the model of a visible sed.
evidence: /home/you/javascript-ch14/first.test.cmd shows `node --test first.test.js` but runs `node --test --test-reporter=spec first.test.js | sed -E 's/ \([0-9.]+ms\)$/ (…ms)/; s/^(ℹ duration_ms) [0-9.]+$/\1 …/'; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. The same pattern is in all 15 *.test.cmd files, stock_up.cmd step 3 (`npm install ../market/sparkle | sed …` shown as `npm install ../market/sparkle`), and run_scripts.cmd steps 4 and 6 (`npm test | sed …; (exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]})`, plus an fd-swapping sed on `npm run manu` stderr). The page discloses this only in prose (P24: 'Times vary on every run, so this book shows (…ms)'; footer) and never in the command. AUTHORING.md house rule 'Timings, PIDs…': 'normalise it visibly in the shown command, e.g. `node --test | sed …`, … as js ch14 does'. The INTEGRATION_TODO 'HIDDEN exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}' item lists only go chapters; js ch14 has it too.
fix: Make each .cmd display string equal the real pipeline, e.g. `node --test first.test.js | sed -E 's/ \([0-9.]+ms\)$/ (…ms)/'`, with `set -o pipefail` as a visible first session step instead of the hidden PIPESTATUS. Either show `--test-reporter=spec` or drop it: Node 26 already defaults to spec when piped (checked locally). Then recapture. Alternatively, reword AUTHORING so it no longer names js ch14 as the example.

panel: 30 (Jigsaw bubble) vs notebook 'Numbers have no limits in JSON'
what: The panel's reason for the BigInt TypeError ('JSON numbers can't promise that much precision') contradicts the notebook, which correctly says JSON numbers have no size limit and JavaScript's parser is what rounds them.

fix: P30: '…JSON.parse on the other end would read it back as an ordinary number and round it, so I refuse instead.'
